pr_title: executor, util: fix spilling disk when oom.
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #16696 

Problem Summary: RowContainer can't spill disk sometimes.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:
1. Add a lock in rowContainer, for Get/Spill mutually exclusive.
2. Add an atomic variable in Tracker.actionMu, to avoid deadlock.

How it Works:

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch 4.0

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test
- Integration test

Side effects

- Performance regression
    - Consumes more CPU

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->
- [Bug-fix] Make spilling disk work well.

comments: Root Cause: A rowContainer has been build and never add chunk again. Then the query uses memory more than quota and actions spill (set `a.c.exceeded = 1`, [code](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/util/chunk/row_container.go#L228)).  But the rowContainer only spill when it add chunk ([code](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/util/chunk/row_container.go#L131)). So it makes the [check](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/util/chunk/row_container.go#L222) always false and block the other spill action.

review_comments: We need to add comment to explain that we need to use `atomic` when trying to modify `spilled`
Should set `c.ptrM.rowPtrs` to `nil` to prevent the unrelease of `SortedRowContainer `.
GetChunk thinks that the data is in memory, but the rowContainer may be spilled to disk.

Currently, the implementation makes `rowContainer` act like random reading, it breaks the OS's block cache and the `ListInDisk`'s `bufio.Reader`.
`ListInDisk.GetChunk` can be implemented so that we can use `GetChunk` here for better performance, besides the `GetChunk` implementation in `RowContainer` can be thread-safe.
add a comment that every partition is a sorted chunk?
All the usage of `alreadySpilled` should be read locked because it touches `c.m.recordsInDisk`
Because `SpillToDisk` may be called after Close happens, this situation should be considered.
Ok, I add RLock in Close().
